answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with a metered paid-service quota bond. Each identity attaches a paid API subscription, and the network draws down a slice of its quota each epoch, a whisper of spend proving it is a funded operation, not a free copy. Quotas are billed per account, so one subscription cannot serve two identities; the quartz-hard check verifies billing fingerprints and remaining quota each round. A Sybil running a hundred clones must buy a hundred subscriptions, so the echo of that cost repeats every epoch, while an honest agent pays once and amortizes it over years of work.
